youtube.title: Which river crosses the Equator twice? Most people guess wrong 🧭
youtube.description:
The Amazon giant, the longest river, or the third one? Only one river on Earth bends north over the Equator and then swings back south across it on its way to the sea. It also drops further below its surface than any other river, and near its end two capital cities stare at each other across the water, the closest pair in the world.
Which did you pick?

research.topic: The Congo River is the only major river to cross the Equator twice: the upper river (Lualaba) flows north across the Equator near Kisangani, the great bend carries it west, and it recrosses the Equator southbound near Mbandaka before reaching the Atlantic (Britannica; NASA Earth Observatory). Length about 4,700 km, second-largest discharge after the Amazon at about 41,000 m³/s (Britannica; USGS). It is the deepest river known: USGS measurements in the lower Congo in 2008 found depths exceeding 220 m (Oberg et al., USGS 2009; Britannica). The Amazon runs mostly a few degrees south of the Equator and the Nile begins near the Equator at Lake Victoria but flows north away from it. Kinshasa (DR Congo) and Brazzaville (Republic of the Congo) face each other across Pool Malebo, the closest pair of national capitals in the world (Britannica).

myths.myth: The Amazon, the biggest river, must be the one on the Equator.
myths.reality: The Amazon runs a few degrees south of the Equator and never crosses it; the Congo crosses it twice because of its great northern bend.
